evidence.claim: Forest roads and a dam crossing connect ancient habitats with the Green River.
evidence.quote: This Byway offers a unique opportunity to interpret wildlife and wildlife habitats both past and present.

evidence.claim: Forest roads and a dam crossing connect ancient habitats with the Green River.
evidence.quote: Flaming Gorge Dam also carries U.S. Route 191 over the river.

evidence.claim: The Flaming Gorge-Uintas National Scenic Byway crosses Ashley National Forest between Manila and Vernal, with a branch over Flaming Gorge Dam toward Wyoming.
evidence.quote: The Flaming Gorge - Uintas National Scenic Byway crosses the Ashley National Forest between the communities of Vernal and Manila. A segment of this Byway also crosses the Flaming Gorge Dam and terminates at the Utah - Wyoming border.

evidence.claim: US 191 climbs through switchbacks into the Uinta Mountains, while SR 44 winds through Sheep Creek Gap.
evidence.quote: It continues north on its climb, encountering several switchbacks

evidence.claim: SR 44 winds through Sheep Creek Gap.
evidence.quote: descending in a series of turns as it approaches the southwestern tip of Flaming Gorge Reservoir and passes through Sheep Creek Gap.

evidence.claim: The Forest Service’s theme, “Wildlife Through The Ages,” connects fossils with living habitats: aspen and pine forests, sandstone formations and streams lined with cottonwoods and willows.
evidence.quote: "Wildlife Through The Ages," is the theme and vision of the Flaming Gorge - Uintas National Scenic Byway.

evidence.claim: aspen and pine forests, sandstone formations and streams lined with cottonwoods and willows.
evidence.quote: forests of aspen, ponderosa, pinyon/juniper and lodgepole pine; sandstone towers and cathedrals; giant red-rock formations; cottonwood and willow lined mountain streams

evidence.claim: The Federal Highway Administration allows two hours for driving, including backtracking on Highway 44, or a day to explore.
evidence.quote: Time to Allow 2 hours (including backtracking on Highway 44) to drive or a day to enjoy the byway.

evidence.claim: A forest highway project linking Vernal and Manila was completed in 1926 and numbered SR 44 in 1927.
evidence.quote: as a forest highway project, completed in 1926, and numbered SR-44 in 1927.

evidence.claim: Dam construction brought the Greendale area its first paved roads in the 1950s and 1960s.
evidence.quote: Major changes came to the Greendale area in the 1950s and 1960s, due to the construction of Flaming Gorge Dam nearby. The region received its first paved roads

evidence.claim: Later realignments changed the route through Ashley National Forest, and in 1981 the stretch south of Greendale Junction became part of US 191.
evidence.quote: Two major realignments through the Ashley National Forest were made in 1966 and 1971

evidence.claim: in 1981 the stretch south of Greendale Junction became part of US 191.
evidence.quote: The final change was in 1981, when the part of SR-44 south of Greendale Junction was renumbered as part of US-191.

evidence.claim: National Scenic Byway designation followed in 1998.
evidence.quote: It was added to the National Scenic Byways system on June 9, 1998.

evidence.claim: Starting at Manila, take SR 44 south through Sheep Creek Gap and east toward Greendale Junction.
evidence.quote: runs from US-191 at Greendale Junction, southwest of Dutch John, to SR-43 in Manila.

evidence.claim: Starting at Manila, take SR 44 south through Sheep Creek Gap and east toward Greendale Junction.
evidence.quote: From this point, the route turns north, exits the recreation area, and continues a few miles further before it ends at the intersection of SR-43 in Manila.

evidence.claim: The US 191 branch crosses the dam and reaches Dutch John before continuing toward Wyoming.
evidence.quote: before crossing Flaming Gorge Dam, and passing by the town of Dutch John.

evidence.claim: before continuing toward Wyoming.
evidence.quote: continuing until the Wyoming state border.

evidence.claim: Return to the junction for the mountain drive south to Vernal, passing Red Fleet and Steinaker state parks.
evidence.quote: passes Steinaker State Park and Red Fleet State Park as it starts to climb into the Uinta Mountains.

evidence.claim: Sheep Creek brings the byway’s wildlife theme close to the road: the Forest Service says bighorn sheep can be seen on the rocky outcrops above the creek.
evidence.quote: bighorn sheep can be seen among the rocky outcrops above Sheep Creek

evidence.claim: Cottonwoods and willows along the stream shelter migrating songbirds.
evidence.quote: the cottonwoods and willows above the stream harbor more species of migrating song birds than any other spot in Utah.

evidence.claim: SR 44 makes a series of turns through Sheep Creek Gap near the reservoir’s southwestern tip.
evidence.quote: descending in a series of turns as it approaches the southwestern tip of Flaming Gorge Reservoir and passes through Sheep Creek Gap.

evidence.claim: A separate route, the Sheep Creek Scenic Backway, crosses the geological area, where the Forest Service highlights twisted, colorful rock formations rising above travelers.
evidence.quote: The Sheep Creek Scenic Backway crosses the highly acclaimed Sheep Creek Geological Area adjacent to the Flaming Gorge National Recreation Area.

evidence.claim: twisted, colorful rock formations rising above travelers.
evidence.quote: views of twisted and colorful geological formations which rise above the traveler

evidence.claim: The creek’s wooded streamside and the rocky outcrops offer two distinct habitats within this part of the drive.
evidence.quote: bighorn sheep can be seen among the rocky outcrops above Sheep Creek, and the cottonwoods and willows above the stream harbor more species of migrating song birds

evidence.claim: Cottonwoods and willows line the creek below rocky outcrops.
evidence.quote: rocky outcrops above Sheep Creek, and the cottonwoods and willows above the stream

evidence.claim: US 191 crosses the Green River on Flaming Gorge Dam, a concrete arch 502 feet high above its foundations.
evidence.quote: The Flaming Gorge Dam stands 502 feet (153 m) high above its foundations

evidence.claim: US 191 crosses the Green River on Flaming Gorge Dam
evidence.quote: Flaming Gorge Dam also carries U.S. Route 191 over the river.

evidence.claim: a concrete arch
evidence.quote: Flaming Gorge Dam is a concrete thin-arch dam on the Green River

evidence.claim: The dam stands in Red Canyon; the gorge that gave it its name lies beneath the reservoir almost 20 miles upstream.
evidence.quote: The canyon, for which the dam is named, is buried under the reservoir almost 20 miles (32 km) upstream.

evidence.claim: The dam stands in Red Canyon
evidence.quote: the dam actually lies in steep, rapid-strewn Red Canyon

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Reclamation built the dam between 1958 and 1964 for a system that stores and distributes upper Colorado River Basin water.
evidence.quote: It was built by the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation between 1958 and 1964.

evidence.claim: a system that stores and distributes upper Colorado River Basin water.
evidence.quote: The dam is a major component of the Colorado River Storage Project, which stores and distributes upper Colorado River Basin water.

evidence.claim: The reservoir submerged four Green River gorges.
evidence.quote: submerging four distinct gorges of the Green River.

evidence.claim: Below the dam, releases are generally colder and clearer than the river’s naturally warm, silty flow, changing its ecology.
evidence.quote: Water released from the dam is generally cold and clear, as compared to the river's naturally warm and silty flow, further changing the local riverine ecology.

evidence.claim: The dam also generates hydroelectric power.
evidence.quote: the dam is also a major source of hydroelectricity

evidence.claim: Dutch John began as housing for the people building Flaming Gorge Dam.
evidence.quote: platted and constructed beginning in 1957 by the United States Bureau of Reclamation to house workers working on the construction of Flaming Gorge Dam.

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Reclamation laid out and began building the town in 1957; during peak construction, as many as 3,500 people lived here.
evidence.quote: During the peak years of construction activity at Flaming Gorge Dam, as many as 3,500 people lived in Dutch John.

evidence.claim: The Bureau of Reclamation laid out and began building the town in 1957
evidence.quote: platted and constructed beginning in 1957 by the United States Bureau of Reclamation

evidence.claim: After the dam was completed in 1964, a smaller community housed dam operations and maintenance staff and federal land-agency employees.
evidence.quote: After the dam's completion in 1964, Dutch John became home to a smaller number of dam maintenance and operations personnel, as well as employees of the National Park Service and United States Forest Service.

evidence.claim: The bureau owned the townsite and buildings until privatization in 1998, when buildings were sold to individual owners and undeveloped land passed to Daggett County.
evidence.quote: The Dutch John townsite and its buildings continued to be owned by the Bureau of Reclamation until 1998 when the town was privatized. Buildings were sold to individual landowners, and undeveloped land in the town was transferred to Daggett County.

evidence.claim: Residents voted to incorporate in 2014, and Dutch John officially became a town in January 2016.
evidence.quote: In November 2014, the residents of Dutch John voted overwhelmingly to incorporate into a town.

evidence.claim: Dutch John officially became a town in January 2016.
evidence.quote: the incorporation became official in January 2016.
